slides.title: Predicting Turn-Taking Outcomes in Multi-Party Conversation: Interpretable Modelling of Speech and Gaze Dynamics with Interpersonal Closeness
slides.highlight: This research models how gaze, speech loudness, and interpersonal closeness signal floor changes in four-person dialogues. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception, specifically addressee identity and listener modeling in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Multimodal models using gaze and speech intensity predict turn-taking gaps or overlaps in multi-party conversations.
card.key_idea: Regularized logistic regression combining speaker loudness, gaze entropy, NMF/PCA-reduced gaze transition motifs, and perceived interpersonal closeness (IOS) to classify floor-transfer outcomes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the GaMMA corpus using LOGO/LOCO cross-validation; the multimodal model achieved ROC AUC of 0.76 ± 0.04, outperforming the gaze-only baseline.

slides.title: Towards a Foundational Ontology for Identifying and Resolving Contradictions in Dialogue-based Human-Robot Interactions
slides.tldr: ONTOLOGY FOR RESOLVING HRI DIALOGUE CONTRADICTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a foundational ontology (ATFOt) to formally represent and resolve contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot interactions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A formal ontology to identify and resolve contradictions in dialogue-based human-robot and human-agent interactions.
card.key_idea: Uses METHONTOLOGY and Activity Theory to represent contradictions (errors, conflicts, knowledge issues) via Set Theory and First Order Logic across four levels of abstraction.
card.evaluation: Preliminary results include natural language, set theoretic, and FoL definitions. Full evaluation via coverage and competency questions is ongoing in Protege.
card.limitation: The work is currently in the preliminary/ongoing stage; the implemented ontology has not yet been qualitatively validated in studies.

slides.title: Humanoid bartender debuts in Hong Kong’s nightlife hub
slides.tldr: HUMANOID BARTENDER DEBUTS IN HONG KONG
slides.highlight: A humanoid bartender has debuted in Hong Kong, demonstrating a real-world application of embodied social robots relevant to RwB.

slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich human-robot interaction in assistive care, emphasizing physics-aware screening over simple task success. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion does not imply physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated against real manikin force-indentation measurements with a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol and physics-aware scoring metrics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs each) using peak force, joint-limit margins, and task success.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue; upper-arm simulation reuses forearm calibration; limited to a single robotic-bathing scenario.

slides.title: From Siena to Beijing, the professor bringing humanoid touch to China
slides.highlight: This item discusses the development of humanoid touch, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees
slides.tldr: CAUSAL REASONING FOR SOCIAL MEDIA SENTIMENT SHIFTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a thread-structured temporal model to analyze how discourse moves drive sentiment shifts in conversation trees, supporting the agent-based social simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: C³T models sentiment shifts in social-media conversation trees using counterfactual reasoning to attribute changes to specific discourse moves.
card.key_idea: A thread-structured Transformer that jointly predicts sentiment and shifts, employs a counterfactual loss for intervention-aware representations, and uses ancestor attention for causal attribution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on rumor datasets against neural and LLM baselines using macro-F1 and Top-1 accuracy; C³T showed superior event-OOD robustness and attribution.
card.limitation: Causal analysis assumes conditional ignorability and treats cross-thread spillovers as a limitation.

slides.title: Leveraging Turn-taking Dynamics for Intent Recognition in Multi-party Conversations
slides.highlight: This work introduces turn-transition entropy to model interaction patterns, supporting HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in multi-party settings.

card.one_liner: A multi-task learning approach improving multi-party intent recognition by predicting turn-taking dynamics via turn-transition entropy.
card.key_idea: Introduces turn-transition entropy as a self-supervised auxiliary regression target to capture speaker interaction predictability, integrated with BERT-like encoders using a weighted geometric mean loss.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MPGT, MIntRec2.0, and MEETInt datasets using macro F1 and accuracy; outperformed baselines including speaker-aware graphs and zero-shot LLMs.
card.limitation: Requires accurate speaker identities for each utterance; performance may degrade if automatic speaker diarization contains errors.

slides.title: Behavior--Realization Separation for Constrained Physical Human--Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: SEPARATING BEHAVIOR SPECIFICATION FROM CONSTRAINED REALIZATION IN pHRI
slides.highlight: This research proposes a layered architecture that separates desired behavior from constrained robot commands, improving precision and torque feasibility in physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposed architecture separates desired interaction behavior from physical robot realization to improve constraint handling.
card.key_idea: A behavior layer provides desired acceleration via an affine interface, while a predictive QP realization layer enforces robot constraints and reports a decomposed realization residual.
card.evaluation: Validated via planar simulations and a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo, comparing predictive realization against reactive clipping for workspace and torque limits.
card.limitation: The predictive runtime is currently validated only for memoryless affine behaviors; nonlinear or stateful specifications may require different machinery.

slides.title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous and Field-Induced Mechanisms of Collective Behavior in One Dimension
slides.tldr: HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION DISCOVERS STATISTICAL PHYSICS THEOREM
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how human-AI collaboration can generate scientific breakthroughs in statistical physics, supporting MIMIC's focus on integrating LLM-based agent models for complex system analysis.

card.one_liner: A human-AI collaboration proves a theorem mapping 1D range-two spin chains to simpler range-one chains.
card.key_idea: A recursive Householder moving-frame transformation maps O(n) and Potts range-two Hamiltonians to range-one models with axial potentials, regardless of interaction functions or system size.
card.evaluation: The theorem was validated by recovering known Ising/XY results and providing a closed-form exact solution for the J1-J2 Potts open chain.
card.limitation: The mapping is specifically proven for open boundary conditions (OBC); periodic or other boundary conditions are not addressed.
